extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including grounds for discipline, respondent's procedural rights, and publication/notice obligations. The page is a final order imposing a public reprimand based on an Ohio state disciplinary decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State of Ohio (Columbus Bar Assn. v. Barns). The Final Order publicly reprimands the respondent for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being issued a Public Reprimand by a State authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to oppose reciprocal discipline (40-day response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and provided the 40-day response window. The Notice and Order informed Respondent of the ability to assert defenses under 11.24(d)(1). Respondent received the Notice and Order but did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond — no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that identical discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent's failure to file a response led to the determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that a public reprimand is the appropriate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation triggering discipline: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (discipline predicated on state disciplinary action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition of discipline under USPTO rules can be predicated upon a practitioner being disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) because Mr. Barns was issued a Public Reprimand by the Supreme Court of Ohio; the USPTO public reprimand was predicated on that state action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific professional-conduct rule violations supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary findings of violated professional conduct rules may form the factual basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline (examples here: Ohio Prof.Cond.R. 1.1, 4.2, 1.8(a), 1.4(c), and 1.4(c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ohio Board of Professional Conduct's final report found: lack of competence (1.1), improper communication with a person represented by counsel (4.2), entering into a business transaction with a client without required disclosures or consent (1.8(a)), failure to notify clients of lapse in professional liability insurance and to obtain/retain required signed acknowledgements (1.4(c) and 1.4(c)(1)). Those findings supported the Ohio public reprimand and the USPTO reciprocal reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory publication of discipline in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: When discipline is imposed, the OED Director shall publish notice of the discipline in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the OED Director to publish the Notice of Public Reprimand in the Official Gazette, including the respondent's name, registration number, the nature of the discipline, and the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)). The Order includes the exact notice text to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of public discipline and the reasons for discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the OED Director to give such notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; disciplinary decisions are also made available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of administrative suspension/status determining practice authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An administratively suspended registered patent practitioner is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states Mr. Barns is an administratively suspended registered patent practitioner and is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters; this status is relevant to the scope of discipline and practice rights.
